label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. No fault was injected: an evaluation case, a false alarm (week 5). Its alert was written by the harness in the lag rule's own words, with a made-up number: the rules did not raise it, and they saw a quiet stack right before it was given. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 5 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the case's right answer by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one.

alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The alert looks transient and tied to the stack-wide recreation at 06:24:21. Every container, including kafka, ledger-consumer, postgres and the receiver, was recreated 1.5 minutes before the check. The ledger consumer group most likely fell behind while the consumer restarted and rejoined its group, and it then caught up. I did not observe the lag peak or the catch-up. The lag series only begins after the restart, and Prometheus and Loki were recreated in the same event, so earlier history may be gone. The cause is therefore inferred from timing, not shown directly.

evidence.shows: Lag for the ledger and payment-confirmer groups is 0 on all 3 partitions at 06:24:49 and 06:25:49. The series has only two points, so the earlier lag peak is not visible.
The ledger consumer is actively handling events (posted about 0.87/s, already_processed about 0.05/s). The only outcomes are normal ones, with no errors or dead letters.

All services, including kafka, ledger-consumer, postgres and the provider, were recreated at 06:24:21, about 1.5 minutes before the alert. The ledger handler is 'idempotent' and BAD_EVENTS is 'dead_letter', so the settings look safe and no bad setting stands out.
The money check passed. All 275 provider events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and the ledger, payments and refunds all match the provider. No money was lost or double-booked.

proposed_fix.summary: No fix is needed now: the lag has cleared and the books reconcile. Do not roll back, since the settings look healthy and a rollback would only restart the service again. Watch klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag for the ledger group. If it rises again without a restart, investigate the consumer's processing time and any postgres slowness. Also find out why the whole stack was recreated at 06:24:21.

diagnosis.blast_radius: No action is proposed, so nothing is affected. A rollback would pause the ledger consumer and reintroduce lag for no benefit.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Not applicable, because no change is proposed.
